blocks.title: One gateway for every model you already pay for
blocks.description: Magpie runs one local gateway in front of every provider you have configured — subscription, API key or local runtime. This plugin connects that gateway to Astravia so its models appear next to the built-in ones.

showcase.user_prompt: Which models does magpie have right now? Pick the longest-context one for this contract.
showcase.assistant_reply: Your gateway answers with 14 models across 3 providers. The largest context is claude-sonnet-4 at 200K tokens, and it takes images as well. It is already in your model list as Magpie — claude-sonnet-4.

items.title: Your real catalog, not a guess
items.description: The panel reads /v1/models from the gateway, so what you see is what magpie can serve right now — with provider, context window, image input and reasoning support.

items.title: One click into the model picker
items.description: Publishing writes the catalog into Astravia's own model registry as an OpenAI-compatible provider. Nothing is written until you press the button, and removing it is one press too.

items.title: Agent tools that read the gateway
items.description: Two read-only tools, magpie_status and magpie_models, let the assistant check whether the gateway is up and which models exist instead of answering from memory.

items.title: Keys stay in magpie
items.description: Your provider credentials live in magpie's own configuration on this computer. The plugin never shows them and never stores them.

items.title: Install magpie if it is not installed yet
items.description: Download it from usemagpie.ai, or run `curl -fsSL https://usemagpie.ai/install.sh | sh`. Add at least one provider inside magpie first — that is where the models come from.

items.title: Start the gateway
items.description: Launch the magpie app, or run `magpie serve`. It listens on 127.0.0.1:3425 by default; if you changed MAGPIE_ADDR, put the address into the panel's connection field instead.

items.title: Open Magpie Gateway and press Publish
items.description: The panel confirms the version and shows the catalog. Publishing adds the models to your model picker; the button right next to it removes them again.

blocks.content: This plugin is a connector, not a runtime: it does not install, start or stop magpie, and it cannot reach the gateway when magpie is not running. The panel says so explicitly instead of failing silently.
